configuration: Six of the eight upstream cases of unittest/joint-composite.cpp over the sixteen joint models of upstream's variant, every operand read from ic/<ic>/operands.json rather than drawn from LieGroupType().randomConfiguration, SE3::Random, Inertia::Random or Eigen's ::Random.
observable: a composite joint against the single joint it is built from, and against two joints that compute the same motion a different way: the placement, motion subspace, velocity and bias from jcalc, the three articulated-body factors and the updated articulated inertia, and the forward kinematics of a ten-joint chain against one composite of the same ten joints
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the operands are frozen rather than drawn
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero component of every frozen item in ic/nominal/operands.json. Perturbing every component rather than one was measured, not assumed: with a single component per item, 18 of cpp-explog's 48 observables and 6 of cpp-spatial's 76 came back with a spread of exactly zero, because a relative change of 2.2e-16 in one entry of a rotation matrix rounds away in the last bit of an output built from all nine. Every component still moves by exactly two units in the last place, so this stays the generic two-ulp noise calibration rather than a physics experiment. A component that is exactly zero is never perturbed, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is a meaningless perturbation of a physical quantity and a parser hazard besides. The worst measured spread is 4.8850e-15 absolute. 64 of the 336 observables show a spread of exactly zero and are insensitive by construction, not by accident. They are the motion subspaces of the axis-aligned joint models, which are constant matrices of zeros and ones independent of the configuration, and the joint biases, which are identically zero for every joint model whose subspace does not itself depend on the configuration; each appears twice, once from the joint and once from the composite. Their bound therefore rests on the physical argument in the warrant rather than on a measured sensitivity, and a reviewer should read it that way.
altbuild: none: the same official.cpp compiled at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off against the same pinned source reproduces the -O2 result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the arithmetic is scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead. The probe was repeated on the worker on 2026-09-14 (x86_64, inside the env image); the result was unchanged, bit-identical.

warrant: The graded quantities are a composite joint against the single joint it is built from, and against two joints that compute the same motion a different way: the placement, motion subspace, velocity and bias from jcalc, the three articulated-body factors and the updated articulated inertia, and the forward kinematics of a ten-joint chain against one composite of the same ten joints, in SI units and in the coordinate order the joint model, the Lie group or the spatial type fixes, which is part of the input and not something an implementation chooses. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 3.28e+00, it admits about 1.03e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this test can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a transposed motion subspace, a rotation composed in the wrong order, a dropped Taylor branch near the identity, a sign error in a cross product or a missing scaling on a mimic joint each move individual values by between 1e-2 and 1e+2 in these units, seven to eleven decades above the bound, and a relative error of one part in a thousand injected into the largest graded value of this check lands 3,180,242 times over it. Every upstream identity also stays active, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these expressions differs by about n eps |x|, roughly 30 * 2.2e-16 * 3.28e+00, which is decades inside the bound. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst of the 4,162 graded values by 4.8850e-15, using 4.862e-06 of the bound, that is 205,671 times of headroom, and the alternative build measured exactly zero. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
